focus: E1 narrowest slice: leaf-manifest generator, fleet freshness gate, and the authoring loop that must re-mint after editing a skill's leaf corpus
noveltyJustification: 6 of 8 findings are new to this research; 2 synthesize repo hook evidence into the root-cause and fix ranking.
ruledOut: pre-commit hook as a new file

label: The leaf generator's --check already byte-compares the committed manifest and its staleness message names the fix command (--write).
The fleet freshness gate regenerates every committed leaf-manifest and fails on byte drift; it is green today (checked=14 fresh=14 failed=0, exit 0, ~9.5s).
The generated-manifest contract is already documented for authors and the reference-only create branch runs the scoped --check, so missing knowledge is not the failure.

The repo pre-commit hook already auto-re-mints two sibling derived families at commit time (compiled-route manifests, spec metadata) and byte-checks Hermes copies, proving the prevention pattern in-repo.
The leaf corpus is excluded from the auto-mint trigger: ROUTE_PATHS names only SKILL.md/hub-router.json/mode-registry.json, so references/assets edits run nothing until CI or push.
The prior __pycache__ fix removed a false-drift producer from the walk but left the mint timing unchanged; probe evidence shows 14/13/1 before and 14/14/0 after.
Root cause: leaf-manifest is a stored derived artifact whose regeneration trigger sits outside the author's edit loop, while every catching gate runs after the edit or on another machine.

Smallest fix ranked by reversal cost: extend the existing pre-commit auto-remint trigger in place to the affected skill's leaf roots and re-mint/stage/confirm leaf-manifest like route manifests; cheaper moves (docs, values) fail and costlier shapes (new file, registry abstraction) are unearned.
